policy: Declaration-only intended Belgian gate posture. Belgium has no incumbent dataset, so incumbent-comparison gates (parity, export_surface, target_surface) are not selected. National and NUTS1 references are declared release-blocking and commune-grain references diagnostic, but this schema change does not wire target-profile tiers or roles into runtime gates. External-oracle implementation (EUROMOD-BE baselines and Federal Planning Bureau reform scores) remains separate work in #264 and is not implemented here.

gates.not_applicable: awaiting d1902: Belgium's per-family fit tolerances (method card BE-MC6) are proposed, not ruled. Shared runner defaults and other countries' numbers may not silently govern Belgium.
gates.notes: Calibration fit per source family so no family hides in the average. Activate when d1902 rules, before any calibrated Belgian candidate. BE-MC6 proposes every calibration target within 5% and demography within 2%; written as NZ wrote its ruled d1376, that is within = hard_within = 0.05, min_family_share = min_hard_family_share = 1 and min_family_size = 1, so a one-target family gates too. Only hard_within, min_hard_family_share and min_family_size decide pass or fail; within and min_family_share are reported.

Intended weighted aggregates against admin anchors on the future hard surface. The tier metadata in target_references.json is declaration-only in this change; a later runner integration must explicitly bridge it into gate tolerances.

gates.not_applicable: Belgium has no commune-grain calibration reference: target_references.json covers the country and NUTS1 levels only, and commune fiscal income waits for a later commune spine gate. No ruling sets a commune tolerance, so aggregate_admin has no anchor to select and no default_rtol to apply.
gates.notes: Commune-grain diagnostics should render per-target fit with the 25 worst-fit communes named; promotion to release_blocking is a spine-quality decision (populace#263), not a default. Activate with commune fiscal-income calibration references, families [fiscal_income], geography_levels [commune] and a ruled default_rtol. aggregate_admin names every anchor that misses default_rtol, with its miss; a ranked worst-25 list that also shows passing communes needs a shared binding parameter first.
The eventual active target profile must cover every named family; the schema declarations and placeholders in this change do not themselves activate that surface.

Authenticate the exact Build P donor artifact and close every declared Frame/Axiom input. A missing substantive root input of any module bound in axiom_rules_bindings.json is a build failure, never an engine default. allow_engine_optional is false: an engine default never closes an input here, and the gate names every engine-optional input it finds. The gate has no evidence before PR 4b: it reads the artifacts of a graph's closure node and donor receipt node, and Belgium has no transport graph yet. evidence_absent_blocks makes that absence block in every posture (docs/gate-battery-contract.md). Until then packages/microcosm-build/tests/engine_free/shared/test_be_axiom_input_closure.py runs the closure's partition on the committed surface.

The US demographics.json / base_population_scale posture against Statbel population structure: age-band x sex x region totals within tight tolerance. families [demography] selects the compiled demography anchors (all NUTS1 today). default_rtol 0.02 is BE-MC6's demography tolerance, proposed and pending d1902, as each demography reference's fit_tolerance also is.
No all-zero stored layers: an all-zero column is a pipeline bug or dead scaffolding masking engine defaults.

No Axiom derived-rule output may persist as a dataset input (a stored engine output masks reforms) — enforced from day one; the adapter's writer refuses such columns and this gate re-checks the artifact. Until Belgium's export contract lists its formula-owned exclusions, formula_owned_columns is every variable a binding in axiom_rules_bindings.json requests, so the gate checks those outputs only.

Physically non-negative columns carry no negatives. columns is the source manifest's nonnegative_outputs (household_weight and age today); incomes and contributions join the list when the source manifest declares them.
Broad release-blocking band against the NBB household-sector anchor — a levels sanity check, not a calibration target (the populace#212 lesson).
